alternatives.concept: Study constitutional, criminal, private, EU, human-rights and public international law alongside transnational business law and cross-border governance. Political institutions, social inquiry and public argument support this legal core; legal research, advice and arbitration exercises provide practical methods, while the full Dutch procedural sequence, specialist research requirements and compulsory legal thesis remain limitations.

candidates.label: French–Dutch legal translation
candidates.reason: The separate specialist route requires French proficiency and French–Dutch legal translation. No current UCR course establishes that language/translation sequence; general stylistics cannot implement it. No independently coherent24course translation programme is established.

candidates.label: European and international legal advocacy
candidates.reason: The strongest available UCR legal, EU, international and rhetoric courses already anchor the closest-match programme. A second advocacy label would retain that core and reshuffle complementary courses without changing its academic priority or producing a substantively different legal curriculum.

routeSelection.basis: Exact programme registry50017 European Law School, now Nederlands, Europees en Internationaal Recht. Current adopted annual OER establishes a complete regular pathway for new2026 entrants without legacy credit substitutions or translator route mixing. Fresh current annual OER and university renaming decision independently confirm this exact target; no legal-translation route substituted.

selection.assessment: One legal-core programme materially addresses the target’s defining Dutch/EU/international subjects, with60EC substantive legal study and specific institutional, trade-governance and justice complements. Current legal advice, comparative contract research, case-law, arbitration and source-based legal interpretation weigh positively; they do not establish a full Dutch procedural programme. The first additional candidate, French–Dutch legal translation, has genuine source support but no French-language/translation implementation in the current workbook. Stylistics offers language analysis, not French acquisition or bilingual legal translation. No independently coherent24course response is established. Advocacy is substantively already integrated through actual legal research, simulatedarbitration,publicargument and rights; reshuffling complements would not establish qualitative distinctness or justify a second curriculum. Stop at one; no forced third alternative.

notes.text: Radboud requires a sustained Dutch civil and procedural sequence, specialist legal research, subject-specific moot courts and a 5-EC legal thesis. This UCR programme provides substantive law, legal case analysis, comparative research and simulated arbitration alongside political and social study. These are meaningful contributions, while the full Dutch requirements and professional legal qualification remain distinct.

audience.programmeDescription: Dutch, European and International Law, formerly European Law School, combines Dutch law with European Union and international law. This comparison follows the regular full-time pathway in the current regulations.
audience.comparisonExplanation: The UCR programme combines substantive constitutional, criminal, private, EU, human-rights, international and transnational business law with cross-border governance, politics and social inquiry. Legal research, advice and simulated arbitration provide practical contributions. It does not reproduce Radboud’s full Dutch civil and procedural sequence, specialist research requirements, criminal/EU moot courts or compulsory legal thesis.

curriculum.limitation: Each year contains 60 EC. The programme requires 176 EC of compulsory study plus one 4-EC restricted metajuridical choice, shown here as Philosophy of Law. There is no open elective space. Noncredit first-year Tutoraat participation and active, prepared participation are additional requirements. The ordinary first-year study-advice threshold is 45 EC. Later-year study requires completion of the first year, or at least 45 EC plus the relevant subject prerequisites. Completing the full first year satisfies that general entry condition.
